The exact Erlang–beta convolution proves the three tail coefficients by exponential tilting, the critical truncated integral, and reverse conditioning. The integer-parameter beta ratio telescopes to independent exponentials for odd d. Checker numerically tested 425,000 directly generated geometrical pairs and independent one-dimensional integrals, but it is not the proof.

value.rationale: The derived observables are the fundamental centered pair-distance distribution and tail in expanding hyperbolic balls, and the natural geodesic distance statistic for high-dimensional hyperbolic graph models. The radial/angular competition yields a sharp three-phase upper-tail boundary, and for every odd hyperbolic dimension genuine volume-uniform sampling has an explicit finite exponential-clock law, with computable full distribution and moments. These characterize an infinite natural dimension family rather than an arbitrary numerical case.
